```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 110
)
pal <- c("#236b83", "#a26421", "#5b8c3a", "#8a3b6b", "#444444", "#b23b3b", "#9aa7b0")
plain <- function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE)
show_bounds <- function(b, note = FALSE) {
  out <- data.frame(path = b$path, lower = plain(b$lower), upper = plain(b$upper),
                    scale = b$scale)
  if (note) out$note <- b$note
  out
}
```

`calibrate_pdm()` searches for parameter values that make simulated flow match observed
flow. Four choices decide how well it does: the **bounds** it searches within, the
**scale** it searches on, the **optimiser** that moves through that space, and the
**objective** that says what "match" means. This article takes each in turn. Multi-start
and computing budgets are covered in [Calibration](calibration.html); the scores themselves
in [Scoring a simulation](scoring.html).

The examples use a storm-driven catchment with a known truth, and Flood Warning set at
3.7 m3/s.

```{r data}
set.seed(8)
n <- 24 * 40
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 3600, length.out = n)
forcing <- data.frame(time = time, pet = 0.04,
                      rain = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.08, stats::rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 4), 0))
truth <- pdm_presets("standard")
truth$area_km2 <- 50
truth$recharge$kg <- 300
truth$distribution$cmax <- 120
run <- function(config) {
  model <- pdm_from_config(config)
  run_pdm(model, forcing, initial_state(model, 0.5))$output$q_m3s
}
observed <- run(truth) * exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.03))
warning_flow <- c(`Flood Warning` = 3.7)
scored <- 241:n # the first ten days are warm-up
```

# How the search works

Every parameter is mapped onto a unit interval, from its lower bound at 0 to its upper bound
at 1, so that parameters measured in millimetres, hours and fractions can be searched
together. The optimiser moves through this unit box; each point it tries is turned back into
parameter values, the model is run, and the objective is scored over the calibration rows.
With several starts, the search begins from several points and the best end point wins.

# Bounds

Bounds should enclose every physically plausible value and nothing else. Too narrow, and the
true value is excluded; too wide, and the search wastes effort on nonsense.
`calibration_bounds()` looks up defaults for every component of a structure from a table
shipped with the package:

```{r bounds}
show_bounds(calibration_bounds(pdm_presets("standard")), note = TRUE)
```

Override any range for a catchment you know, add a parameter, or hold one fixed:

```{r overrides}
b <- calibration_bounds(pdm_presets("standard"),
                        overrides = list(fc = c(0.9, 1.2), td = c(0, 3)),
                        exclude = "groundwater.kb")
show_bounds(b)
```

# Search scale

The recharge constant `kg` may sensibly lie anywhere from about 1 to 5,000 hours. Searched
evenly, the whole range from 1 to 50 hours, where many responsive catchments sit, is 1 per
cent of the search space. Searched on a log scale, each tenfold step gets equal room.

```{r scale, fig.cap="Twenty random starting values for kg between 1 and 5,000 hours, drawn evenly (top) and on a log scale (bottom), plotted on a log axis.", fig.height=2.2}
set.seed(1)
even <- stats::runif(20, 1, 5000)
logged <- exp(stats::runif(20, log(1), log(5000)))
par(mar = c(4, 6, 0.6, 0.6))
plot(c(even, logged), rep(2:1, each = 20), log = "x", pch = 16, col = pal[1], yaxt = "n",
     ylim = c(0.5, 2.5), xlab = "kg (hours, log axis)", ylab = "", xlim = c(1, 5000))
axis(2, at = 2:1, labels = c("even", "log scale"), las = 1)
```

On an example where the true `kg` is 40 hours, starting from 1,000:

```{r scale-run}
flat <- pdm_presets("standard")
flat$recharge$kg <- 40
flat_obs <- run(flat)
start <- flat
start$recharge$kg <- 1000
args <- list(start, forcing, flat_obs, lower = c(recharge.kg = 1), upper = c(recharge.kg = 5000),
             warmup = 240, objective = "nse", control = list(maxit = 50))
even_fit <- do.call(calibrate_pdm, args)
log_fit <- do.call(calibrate_pdm, c(args, list(log_scale = "recharge.kg")))
data.frame(scale = c("even", "log"),
           kg = round(c(even_fit$parameters, log_fit$parameters), 2),
           model_runs = c(sum(even_fit$start_results$evaluations),
                          sum(log_fit$start_results$evaluations)))
```

Both find it; the log-scale search takes a fraction of the model runs. The bounds table
marks which parameters to search this way, and `compare_structures()` uses it
automatically. With `calibrate_pdm()` and `log_auto_calibration()`, name them in `log_scale`.

# Optimisers

`calibrate_pdm()` offers two.

| Method | How it moves | Suits | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lbfgsb` (default) | Follows the slope of the objective, estimated from small steps | Smooth objectives: NSE, RMSE, log RMSE | Fewest model runs |
| `nelder_mead` | Moves a simplex of points by comparing their values, no slopes | Objectives with steps or flat stretches | Several times more runs |

The difference matters because some scores are not smooth. NSE changes a little for every
small change of a parameter. CSI counts events, so it stays exactly the same until a
simulated peak crosses the threshold, and then jumps.

```{r profiles, fig.cap="The two objectives along one parameter, the first surface time constant, with everything else at the truth. NSE changes smoothly; CSI at Flood Warning is a staircase."}
grid <- seq(1.5, 6, length.out = 60)
profile <- t(vapply(grid, function(k) {
  cfg <- truth
  cfg$surface$k1 <- k
  sim <- run(cfg)[scored]
  c(nse = pdm_scorecard(sim, observed[scored])[["nse"]],
    csi = pdm_threshold_scores(sim, observed[scored], warning_flow)$csi)
}, numeric(2)))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.2, 1.5, 0.8))
plot(grid, profile[, "nse"], type = "l", lwd = 2, col = pal[1], xlab = "surface.k1 (hours)",
     ylab = "NSE", main = "Smooth", cex.main = 0.95)
plot(grid, profile[, "csi"], type = "s", lwd = 2, col = pal[2], xlab = "surface.k1 (hours)",
     ylab = "CSI at Flood Warning", main = "Steps", cex.main = 0.95)
```

On a flat stretch the slope is zero, so a gradient method has nothing to follow and stops
where it started; at a step, the slope it estimates is meaningless. Nelder-Mead only compares
values, so it can cross the flats. pdmS7 runs Nelder-Mead on a logistic transform of the unit
box, so every point it tries stays inside the bounds.

# Objectives

The objective is what the optimiser is rewarded for:

| `objective` | Minimises | Emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| `nse` | 1 - NSE | Floods; the usual default |
| `rmse` | Root mean square error, m3/s | Floods, in flow units |
| `log_rmse` | RMSE of log flows | Low flows |
| `threshold` | The threshold term alone | Threshold crossings only |

## Rewarding threshold skill

A model for a warning service should cross the warning threshold when the river does.
`calibrate_pdm()` can add a threshold term to the continuous objective:

> objective = (1 - NSE) + weight × mean over thresholds of (1 - CSI)

The continuous part keeps a slope everywhere and breaks ties between parameter sets with the
same CSI; the threshold part rewards getting the crossings right. Because the sum has steps,
it needs Nelder-Mead.

```{r threshold-fit}
start <- truth
start$fc <- 0.9
start$surface$k1 <- 4
start$surface$k2 <- 7
lower <- c(fc = 0.7, surface.k1 = 0.5, surface.k2 = 0.5)
upper <- c(fc = 1.4, surface.k1 = 20, surface.k2 = 20)
common <- list(start, forcing, observed, lower, upper, warmup = 240, objective = "nse",
               log_scale = c("surface.k1", "surface.k2"), starts = 2, seed = 1)
nse_only <- do.call(calibrate_pdm, common)
with_threshold <- do.call(calibrate_pdm, c(common, list(
  method = "nelder_mead", thresholds = warning_flow, threshold_weight = 1,
  control = list(maxit = 300)
)))
summarise <- function(fit) {
  sim <- run(fit$config)[scored]
  events <- pdm_threshold_scores(sim, observed[scored], warning_flow)
  c(round(fit$parameters, 2), nse = round(pdm_scorecard(sim, observed[scored])[["nse"]], 4),
    csi = round(events$csi, 2), crossing_error_h = round(events$crossing_error_h, 2),
    model_runs = sum(fit$start_results$evaluations))
}
rbind(nse_only = summarise(nse_only), with_threshold = summarise(with_threshold))
with_threshold$objective_name
```

Here the threshold term catches the remaining Flood Warning event at almost no cost in NSE,
for about twice the model runs. That is the typical bargain: a small change in parameters,
chosen with the warning in mind, rather than a different model.

Some guidance:

- **Weight.** NSE and CSI both run from about 0 to 1 for useful models, so a weight of 1 is a
  neutral start. Larger weights favour crossings over the hydrograph as a whole.
- **Events.** A threshold the river crosses only once or twice gives the optimiser almost
  nothing to work with, and the result can be luck. `calibrate_pdm()` refuses a threshold
  never crossed in the calibration period.
- **Other scores.** `threshold_score` may be `pod`, `far`, or a step-based score such as
  `ets_step`; false alarm ratios are minimised directly.
- **Gradient methods refuse.** A threshold term with `method = "lbfgsb"` is an error, with
  the reason.

# In a calibration project

`log_auto_calibration()` runs the same search on a project's registered data and windows,
using the thresholds registered with the data by name, and records everything a reviewer
needs to repeat it: bounds, search scales, method, objective and weights, starts and seed,
every start's result, the number of model runs, and the reasoning.

```{r logged, eval=FALSE}
log_auto_calibration(
  project, parent = 7,
  lower = c(fc = 0.7, surface.k1 = 0.5, surface.k2 = 0.5),
  upper = c(fc = 1.4, surface.k1 = 20, surface.k2 = 20),
  log_scale = c("surface.k1", "surface.k2"), starts = 4, seed = 1,
  method = "nelder_mead", threshold_objective = "Flood Warning", threshold_weight = 1,
  reasoning = "Tune the surface stores for warning timing."
)
```

# Choosing

| Situation | Settings |
|---|---|
| First calibration of a catchment | `objective = "nse"`, default method, several starts, bounds from `calibration_bounds()`, log scale where marked |
| Low flows matter | `objective = "log_rmse"` |
| A warning service | Add `thresholds` with `method = "nelder_mead"`; keep a continuous objective |
| Several structures | `compare_structures()`, which applies all of the above alike; see [Choosing a model structure](choosing-structure.html) |
| Many catchments | One protocol for all; see [Calibrating many catchments](many-catchments.html) |
